To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the SRL conceptual model is a valid and reliable framework for understanding student motivation and learning, (b) SRL and SAL constructs are distinct, (c) SRL constructs are related to learning and achievement, and (d) SRL constructs may be used to predict student learning and achievement.

(1) the conceptual framework for assessing college student motivation and SRL is based on a SRL perspective and (2) the conceptual framework may be used to guide the development of instruments that assess student motivation and learning.

(1) the SRL framework is a more useful conceptualization of student motivation and learning than the SAL framework; (2) students' self-efficacy beliefs are a better predictor than students' learning goals of their self-regulated learning; and (3) students' self-regulatory strategies and processes are more strongly associated with academic achievement than are students' learning goals and self-efficacy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive conceptual framework for understanding the motivational and cognitive processes involved in college student learning.
understanding the role of motivation and self-regulatory processes in learning and achievement in the college classroom.
the study of motivation and self-regulation of learning in college students and the implications of this research for the design and implementation of instruction.

a self-regulatory approach is more useful than an approaches to learning approach in understanding and measuring college student motivation and self regulated learning.
the SRL framework provides an effective way to understand the motivational processes underlying college student learning.
the SRL conceptualization of student motivation and learning is an important theoretical and research framework for understanding and assessing college student learning.

the SRL framework provides a useful conceptual framework for understanding the motivational and cognitive processes that underlie learning in college.
the SRL perspective provides a more comprehensive and coherent view of the motivational and cognitive aspects of student learning.

the self-regulatory conceptual framework provides an effective and efficient way of organizing and interpreting the literature on college student motivation, self-regulated learning, and approaches to learning.

a SRL approach may be more useful than a SAL approach for understanding and assessing college student motivation and self regulated learning.
the conceptual framework for SRL and motivation in college students can be useful in guiding the development of instruments that can be used to assess college student learning and motivation.

college student motivation is best understood as an interaction between students' self-regulation and the classroom context, rather than as a set of student characteristics that are independent of context.
